title: [pickle][MutableDict] SA gets confused on which MutableDict has been updated after pickling instance

labels.name: sqlalchemy.ext
labels.description: extension modules, most of which are ORM related

body:
### Describe the bug

I have a model with 2 `sqlalchemy.ext.mutable.MutableDict` as properties. After pickling an instance, if I update one of the `dict`, the **last** one defined in the model gets its key added to `commited_state` no matter which one it was.

### To Reproduce

```python
import pickle
from typing import Any, Dict, Optional

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, PickleType, create_engine, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import registry, Session
from sqlalchemy.ext.mutable import MutableDict

mapper_registry = registry()


@mapper_registry.mapped
@dataclass
class User:
    __tablename__ = "user"
    __sa_dataclass_metadata_key__ = "sa"
    id: int = field(init=False, metadata={"sa": Column(Integer, primary_key=True)})

    # order matter here (if you invert the dict declarations, the assertion bellow passes)
    foo2_metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = field(
        default_factory=dict,
        metadata={"sa": Column(MutableDict.as_mutable(PickleType))},
    )

    foo1_metadata: Dict[str, Any] = field(
        default_factory=dict,
        metadata={"sa": Column(MutableDict.as_mutable(PickleType), nullable=False)},
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(mapper_registry.metadata.tables)

    engine = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True, future=True)
    mapper_registry.metadata.create_all(engine)

    user = User()
    print("Commited state before add:", user._sa_instance_state.committed_state)

    with Session(engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:
        session.add(user)
        session.commit()

    with Session(engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:
        user_bis = session.scalar(select(User).where(User.id == user.id))
        assert user_bis is not None

    assert len(user_bis._sa_instance_state.committed_state) == 0

    user_bis.foo2_metadata["bar"] = 42

    # should be fine here
    assert "foo2_metadata" in user_bis._sa_instance_state.committed_state

    # retry with pickling of the instance
    with Session(engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:
        user_bis = session.scalar(select(User).where(User.id == user.id))
        assert user_bis is not None

    user_bis = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(user_bis))
    assert len(user_bis._sa_instance_state.committed_state) == 0

    user_bis.foo2_metadata["bar"] = 42

    # fails there (it has "foo1_metadata" instead)
    assert "foo2_metadata" in user_bis._sa_instance_state.committed_state
```

### Versions

- OS: Linux (Ubuntu 20.04)
- Python: tested with 3.6 & 3.9 (others might also be concerned)
- SQLAlchemy: 1.4.36
- Database: SQLite 3.31.1
- DBAPI (eg: psycopg, cx_oracle, mysqlclient): [pysqlite](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/dialects/sqlite.html#module-sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite.pysqlite)
